Covert

KOH-vurt — rhymes with 'over' plus a 't'; a covert operation stays quietly 'covered' from view. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Covert is secret or not openly displayed.

The company launched a covert investigation into the missing funds without alerting any employees.

Worked Example

A store manager suspects an employee of theft. Instead of confronting him directly, she quietly reviews security footage after hours and asks a trusted coworker to keep an unannounced eye on the register, all without the suspect ever knowing he's being watched.

Carrying out an investigation secretly, without anyone knowing it's happening, is exactly what covert means. Unlike 'obvious,' which is easy to notice, covert means deliberately hidden from view.

How Covert Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

secret

secret: kept hidden from others

clandestine

clandestine: done secretly, often because it is illicit

undercover

undercover: working secretly to gather information

Antonyms

overt

overt: done openly, not hidden

public

public: open and known to everyone

How Strong Is It? — quiet → covert → clandestine

quiet vs. covert

quiet vs. covert: Quiet is weaker than covert — something quiet just avoids drawing attention, while covert is deliberately kept secret and hidden from view.

clandestine vs. covert

clandestine vs. covert: Clandestine can feel even more secretive than covert: covert simply means hidden, but clandestine often implies the secrecy exists because the activity is illicit or forbidden.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — covert-

root — covert-: covered, hidden (Old French/Latin (cooperire, 'to cover completely'))

Put it together

Put it together: Covert comes from Old French covert, the past participle of covrir ('to cover'), itself from Latin cooperire. At its root, something covert is simply kept 'covered' from view.
